newsitem.title: FRANCE: Tapie's health forces new break in trial.
newsitem.headline: Tapie's health forces new break in trial.

text.p: Flamboyant Frenchman Bernard Tapie's trial on embezzlement charges was suspended again on Thursday after the bankrupt ex-tycoon and former soccer boss turned ashen in court and was rushed to hospital.
"You are looking worse and worse. Are you sure you are all right?" judge Guy Richarte asked Tapie after a break in the testimony.
When Tapie gave an evasive look, the judge ordered an emergency ambulance crew to evacuate him from the courtroom and suspended proceedings.
It was the second day in a row that the trial had been suspended.
Tapie, who is 54, spent 19 hours in a coronary intensive care unit on Wednesday after waking in the middle of the night with chest pains and breathing difficulties.
The trial resumed on Thursday morning after the court concluded that his health was not in jeopardy.
Tapie, former boss of soccer club Marseille, is standing trial in the Mediterranean port city while serving an earlier jail sentence for fixing a match.

He went to prison nearly four months ago after the supreme court upheld an eight-month sentence for bribing players of league rival Valenciennes to give Marseille an easy game, days before Marseille beat AC Milan in the 1993 European Cup final.
In the current case, which opened on May 12, he is charged with embezzling 100 million francs ($17.5 million) from the Marseille club.
Nineteen other soccer figures are standing trial along with Tapie in the case, which is expected to last another two weeks.
He faces a five-year sentence if convicted on the charges of swindling, misusing corporate funds and falsifying documents between 1987 and 1993.
